newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army said to kill 30 rebels, detain 15.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army said to kill 30 rebels, detain 15.

text.p: The Burundi army killed 30 Hutu rebels and detained 15 in an operation in the volatile Cibitoke area, military sources said on Monday.
They said the killings followed an army clash with the rebels, former soldiers of the Rwandan and former Zaire armies and Rwandan ethnic Hutu Interahamwe militia last week.
They added that fighting continued in Mabayi, Mogina and Mogwi communes, northwest of Burundi's capital Bujumbura.

The military sources said top officers of the armies of Burundi and Rwanda met at the weekend and the Rwandan army said Interahamwe and former soldiers planned to enter the Nyungwe forest from where they would intensify their campaign.

The Rwandans said the former soldiers had hidden most of their weapons in the forest as they fled in 1994 after the slaughter of an estimated 800,000 ethnic Tutsis and moderate Hutus, according to the Burundi military sources.
"(Hutu) rebels are circling around Cibitoke and it is hard to say whether these attacks will end," an army officer said.
"Rebels move around like water in the ocean. You hit one area and find they have already moved to the next," he added.
The U.N. refugee agency estimates that some 100,000 people have been displaced by the fighting in the Cibitoke province.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war since October 1993, when the country's first elected Hutu president was murdered by Tutsi troops.

Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army arrested 14 students last Wednesday during a university sit-in protest against Buyoya's decision to negotiate with the rebels. Both sides signed a pre-ceasefire agreement after secret talks in Rome.
